heroHeadline: Trump-Xi Summit Concludes with No Taiwan Statement; Arms Sales Fate Uncertain; PLA Re-Escalates to 15 Aircraft on Summit Conclusion Day; HIMARS Deadline 16 Days Away
heroSubtitle: The Trump-Xi Beijing summit concluded on May 15, 2026 without a joint communiqué on Taiwan and with profound ambiguity about the $14 billion US arms package. Xi Jinping's defining warning — 'Handle Taiwan badly and the two countries risk collision or conflict' — stood unaddressed by the US side, and the American readout contained no mention of Taiwan. Secretary of State Rubio stated that arms sales 'did not feature prominently' in Trump's talks with Xi, alarming bipartisan congressional Taiwan hawks. Bloomberg headlined the post-summit moment: 'Trump and Xi Had a Warm Summit. Taiwan Will Test Ties Soon.' PLA marked the summit's conclusion day with a post-summit re-escalation: 15 aircraft detected around Taiwan (2 entering SW ADIZ) as of the May 15 06:00 snapshot — the highest total aircraft count since May 7's 22-sortie surge, sharply up from summit window lows of 2-3 sorties. The full May sortie sequence now reads: 4→29→1→2→1→0→22→12→8→12→7→9→2→3→15. Taiwan's HIMARS payment deadline (May 31) is now just 16 days away; Taiwan's MND confirmed it is prepared to use reserve funds if the legislature does not approve timely disbursement. The $14B PAC-3/NASAMS package remains on formal hold pending Trump's post-summit decision.
